reviewed_controls.control: repair-render uses the shared queue lock and reads the latest source while locked
state reads and atomic writes reject symlinked parent and leaf paths using directory file descriptors and no-follow opens
active claim scopes are preflighted for symlinks and non-regular files; instruction discovery rejects scoped symlink escapes
mutations check the implementation branch and current subject inside the queue lock; CAS and filesystem preflights are in the locked update path
source and generated view use file and parent-directory fsync; source-first partial failure is detected by exact rendered-view validation
strict JSON/schema, canonical UTC timestamps, path overlap, priority, dependency reservation, expiry handoff history, and shared API ownership checks remain enforced
verification binds the raw external review file hash and current allowed-path digest to the subject recorded in accepted source

approval_limits: This approval covers only the two listed file-content hashes. The staged tree, parent/tree identity, and binary diff digest were not supplied; a separate review must bind the eventual frozen staged subject and commit.
The request reported 34 focused tests passing. I inspected the test source but did not run tests or builds; no Cargo command was run.
Reviewer identity is stored as text and is not cryptographically authenticated by this tool, as its module documentation states.

Filesystem-scope checks are mutation-time preflights, not an OS sandbox; an owner can change files or introduce a symlink after preflight. Instruction discovery is explicitly static-only and does not prove runtime instruction loading.
The queue review does not qualify product behavior, visual parity, or the validity of evidence asserted by task owners.
